name: Perugu Vada
subtitle: urad dal vadas soaked soft and drowned in seasoned yogurt
prepNotes: Grind the dal with as little water as possible. A wet batter gives flat, oily vadas.
The soak in warm water after frying is what makes them spongy. Skip it and you get bread in yogurt.

steps.text: Drain the dal and grind to a thick, fluffy paste, adding water a spoonful at a time. Beat it by hand for 2 minutes to aerate.
steps.tip: A spoonful of batter dropped in water should float. If it sinks, beat it more.

steps.text: Mix in the green chilli, ginger and salt. Shape into flat rounds with a hole in the middle and fry until golden.
Drop the hot vadas into warm salted water for 10 minutes, then squeeze each one gently between your palms.
steps.tip: Gently. You are pressing out water, not flattening them.

steps.text: Season the yogurt with salt and pour it over the squeezed vadas. Refrigerate at least an hour.
Heat 2 tbsp oil, splutter the mustard and cumin seeds with the dried chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida, and pour it over. Finish with coriander.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. The vadas go on drinking the yogurt, so add a few spoonfuls of fresh whisked yogurt before serving on day two.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
